quick: Generally considered low risk; use if needed
summary: Loratadine is a long-acting, non-sedating second-generation H1 antihistamine for allergic rhinitis and chronic urticaria. The usual adult dose is 10 mg once daily. It has minimal sedation and anticholinergic effect at recommended doses, making it suitable for daytime use.
indications: Symptomatic relief of seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis (runny nose, sneezing, itchy/watery eyes, nasal/throat itch)
Chronic idiopathic urticaria (relief of itching and hives)

dosage.n: Not more than 10 mg in 24 hours
Higher off-label doses sometimes used under specialist care

admin: Take orally once daily, with or without food
Orally disintegrating tablets: place on tongue and let dissolve, no water needed
Use the measured syrup for children
Do not exceed one dose in 24 hours
Consult a doctor before use in significant liver or kidney disease
moa: Loratadine is a selective peripheral histamine H1-receptor antagonist. By blocking H1 receptors it inhibits the effects of histamine released in allergic reactions, reducing vascular permeability, itching, sneezing and rhinorrhea. Poor CNS penetration accounts for its low sedative effect.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to loratadine or any excipient
relative: Rare hereditary galactose intolerance (some tablet formulations)

preg: Human data have not shown an increased risk of malformations; loratadine is generally considered one of the preferred antihistamines in pregnancy when treatment is needed. Use if clearly required.
lact: Loratadine and its metabolite are excreted in breast milk in small amounts and it is considered compatible with breastfeeding. Monitor the infant for unusual drowsiness.
renal: In severe renal impairment (GFR <30 mL/min) reduce dosing frequency, e.g. 10 mg every other day.
hepatic: In hepatic impairment, clearance is reduced; use a lower starting frequency such as 10 mg every other day.

moderate: Strong CYP3A4/CYP2D6 inhibitors (ketoconazole, erythromycin, cimetidine) - raise loratadine levels, usually without clinical effect
Other QT-prolonging drugs - theoretical additive risk at high doses
interactions.food: No clinically significant food interaction; food may slightly delay absorption.
interactions.alcohol: Minimal interaction at recommended doses; avoid excess.
interactions.diagnostics: May suppress skin-prick (allergy) test responses - withhold for several days before testing.

counsel: Take one 10 mg dose once daily and do not exceed it
Drowsiness is uncommon but possible - see how it affects you before driving
Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney disease
Stop antihistamines several days before any allergy skin test
Seek urgent care for facial swelling or difficulty breathing
pearls: Non-sedating at 10 mg - preferred for daytime allergy control
Active metabolite desloratadine gives a long 24-hour duration
One of the antihistamines considered safer in pregnancy and lactation
Reduce frequency in hepatic or severe renal impairment
Withhold before skin-prick allergy testing to avoid false negatives
missed: If you take it regularly and miss a dose, take it when remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one. Do not take two doses within 24 hours.
overdose: Overdose may cause somnolence, headache, tachycardia and, in children, extrapyramidal signs. Treatment is supportive with gastric decontamination if early; loratadine is not removed by hemodialysis. Monitor cardiac rhythm with large ingestions.
